The Information System Security Officer (ISSO) will verify that a baseline configuration document exists, is current, and that changes to the system are processed through the organization's configuration control board.
If no current baseline configuration document exists, this is a finding.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: RHEL 8 must be located in a controlled access area.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>Physical access controls are a prerequisite to every logical control the operating system implements.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext: Relocate the system to a controlled access area meeting the physical security requirements for its classification level, or obtain a documented risk acceptance from the Authorizing Official.

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Verify the system is located in a controlled access area.
Inspect the physical location of the system. The Information System Security Officer (ISSO) will confirm the area meets the physical security requirements for the system's classification level.
If the system is not located in a controlled access area, this is a finding.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: RHEL 8 users must be trained on the acceptable use policy before being granted access.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>Organizations are required to ensure users are aware of their responsibilities before granting access.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext: Ensure every user completes acceptable use training before an account is created, and retain the training records for the life of the account.

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Verify all users with accounts on the system have completed acceptable use training.
Ask the System Administrator for training records. The Information System Security Officer (ISSO) will verify records exist for every interactive account on the system.
If training records are missing for any account, this is a finding.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: RHEL 8 must take appropriate action when an audit processing failure occurs and notify designated personnel.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>It is critical for the appropriate personnel to be aware if a system is at risk of failing to process audit logs as required.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext: Document the audit processing failure notification procedure, identify the designated personnel by role, and obtain ISSO approval.

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Verify that designated personnel are notified when an audit processing failure occurs.
Ask the System Administrator to identify the designated personnel and demonstrate how they are notified. Review the notification procedure with the Information System Security Officer (ISSO).
If there is no documented notification procedure, or the designated personnel are not identified, this is a finding.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: RHEL 8 must have an approved contingency plan for restoring the system after a failure.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>Without a contingency plan, restoration of the system after a failure is unlikely to meet the organization's recovery time objective.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext: Develop a contingency plan for the system, test it annually, document the results, and obtain ISSO approval.

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Verify an approved contingency plan exists for the system.
The Information System Security Officer (ISSO) will verify the plan is current, has been tested within the last year, and that the test results are documented.
If no current, tested contingency plan exists, this is a finding.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: RHEL 8 must automatically lock an account until the locked account is released by an administrator when three unsuccessful logon attempts occur during a 15-minute time period.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>By limiting the number of failed logon attempts, the risk of unauthorized system access via user password guessing is reduced.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext:
Configure the operating system to lock an account until released by an administrator when three unsuccessful logon attempts occur in 15 minutes.
Add/Modify the "/etc/security/faillock.conf" file to match the following line:
unlock_time = 0
Note: If a centralized account management method is in use, apply the equivalent setting there instead; the local file will not be authoritative.

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Note: If the system administrator (SA) demonstrates the use of an approved centralized account management method that locks an account after three unsuccessful logon attempts within a period of 15 minutes, this requirement is Not Applicable.
Check that the system locks an account after three unsuccessful logon attempts within a period of 15 minutes with the following commands:
$ sudo grep 'unlock_time =' /etc/security/faillock.conf unlock_time = 0
If the "unlock_time" option is not set to "0", is missing or commented out, this is a finding.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: All RHEL 8 local interactive user accounts must be assigned a home directory upon creation.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>If local interactive users are not assigned a valid home directory, there is no place for the storage and control of files they should own.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext:
Configure RHEL 8 to assign home directories to all new local interactive users by setting the "CREATE_HOME" parameter in "/etc/login.defs" to "yes":
CREATE_HOME yes
If home directories are provisioned by a directory service, configure the equivalent setting there instead.

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Verify all local interactive users on RHEL 8 are assigned a home directory upon creation with the following command:
$ sudo grep -i create_home /etc/login.defs CREATE_HOME yes
If the value for "CREATE_HOME" parameter is not set to "yes", the line is missing, or the line is commented out, this is a finding.
Note: If the site uses a directory service that provisions home directories on a fileserver, determine with the System Administrator whether CREATE_HOME is the correct control point for this system.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: RHEL 8 audit logs must have a mode of 0600 or less permissive to prevent unauthorized read access.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>Unauthorized disclosure of audit records can reveal system and configuration data to attackers.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext:
Configure the audit logs to be protected from unauthorized read access by setting the correct permissive mode with the following command, substituting the audit log path from "auditd.conf":
$ sudo chmod 0600 /var/log/audit/*

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Verify the audit logs have a mode of "0600" or less permissive.
First determine where the audit logs are stored with the following command:
$ sudo grep -iw log_file /etc/audit/auditd.conf log_file = /var/log/audit/audit.log
Using the location of the audit log file, check if each audit log has a mode of "0600" or less permissive with the following command, substituting the correct audit log path:
$ sudo stat -c "%a %n" /var/log/audit/* 600 /var/log/audit/audit.log
If the audit logs have a mode more permissive than "0600", this is a finding.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: The RHEL 8 file system automounter must be disabled unless required.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>Automatically mounting file systems permits easy introduction of unknown devices, thereby facilitating malicious activity.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext:
Configure the operating system to disable the ability to automount devices.
If autofs is not required for the mission:
$ sudo systemctl mask --now autofs
If autofs is required, document the requirement and obtain ISSO approval instead of disabling it.

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Verify the operating system disables the ability to automount devices.
Note: If the autofs service is required for the system's documented mission, and its use is approved by the Information System Security Officer (ISSO), this requirement is Not Applicable.
Check that the autofs service is disabled with the following command:
$ sudo systemctl is-enabled autofs disabled
If the autofs service is enabled and is not documented as an operational requirement, this is a finding.

xccdf:Rule.xccdf:title: RHEL 8 must not enable IPv6 packet forwarding unless the system is a router.
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:description: <VulnDiscussion>Routing protocol daemons are typically used on routers to exchange network topology information with other routers.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
xccdf:Rule.xccdf:fixtext:
Configure RHEL 8 to not allow IPv6 packet forwarding, unless the system is a router.
Add or edit the following line in a system configuration file in the "/etc/sysctl.d/" directory:
net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 0
Load settings from all system configuration files with the following command:
$ sudo sysctl --system
If the system is a router, this requirement is Not Applicable and the setting must not be changed.

xccdf:check.xccdf:check-content:
Verify RHEL 8 is not performing IPv6 packet forwarding, unless the system is a router.
Note: If IPv6 is disabled on the system, this requirement is Not Applicable.
Check that IPv6 forwarding is disabled with the following command:
$ sudo sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 0
If the returned line does not have a value of "0", or a line is not returned, and the system is not a router, this is a finding.
